sources.title: Llama-3.2-1B-Instruct model card
sources.evidence: Exact Instruct repository: Meta developer; text-only multilingual chat; 1B (1.23B), GQA and shared embeddings; original 128k versus quantized 8k; September 25, 2024 release. Reopened October 27: retains 1B (1.23B), and explicitly describes tuned versions as SFT/RLHF aligned.

sources.title: Llama 3.2 launch announcement
sources.evidence: September 25, 2024 launch includes 1B instruction-tuned BF16 weights for edge/mobile use. Structured pruning from Llama 3.1 8B and distillation using 8B/70B logits precede chat alignment.

sources.title: Official Llama model SKU definitions
sources.evidence: Exact meta-llama/Llama-3.2-1B-Instruct SKU uses arch_args_1b: dimension 2048, 16 layers, 32 attention heads and 8 KV heads. INT4 QLoRA/SpinQuant are separately identified variants. Reopened October 27: the base 1B and original Instruct definitions have the same architecture dimensions; separate QLoRA variants add LoRA configuration.

sources.title: Official model types and context limits
sources.evidence: BF16 is the default checkpoint format. Llama 3.2 max_seq_length returns 131072 except INT4, which returns 8192.

sources.title: Official Llama Transformer implementation
sources.evidence: Causal Transformer blocks execute attention and three dense feedforward projections in every layer; no expert routing. Attention repeats grouped KV heads; the feedforward uses SiLU gating.

sources.title: Llama 3.2 model cards and prompt formats
sources.evidence: Tool Calling (1B/3B) explicitly supports custom function definitions in system/user prompts, excluding built-in Brave Search and Wolfram. Quantized Instruct variants arrived after original BF16 models and have 8k context.

sources.title: Exact checkpoint public repository metadata
sources.evidence: Public metadata at revision 9213176726f574b556790deb65791e0c5aa438b6 exposes LlamaForCausalLM and the exact JSON function-call chat template, restricted to single calls. BF16 aggregate is 1,235,814,400 storage elements; tensor shapes were not independently inspected.

sources.title: Llama 3.2 Community License Agreement
sources.evidence: Names the custom Llama 3.2 Community License and September 25, 2024 version release date; distributes trained weights subject to its conditions.

sources.title: Exact checkpoint configuration access check
sources.evidence: Unauthenticated access returned HTTP 401. No gate bypass or weight download was attempted; public SKU metadata supplies the needed architecture/context evidence.

sources.title: Shared Llama 3.2 model card, updated for quantization
sources.evidence: Current shared card includes BF16 and quantized variants and states October 24, 2024. That date conflicts with the exact original checkpoint card and September launch; it is not used as original BF16 release date.

sources.title: Models.dev source record
sources.evidence: Baseline catalog asserts tool support, no reasoning support, and 131072 context. These were treated as leads and checked against primary evidence.

sources.title: Meta Llama 3.2 reference text prompt formats
sources.evidence: Explicitly describes pythonic function calls for 1B and3B Instruct and supports multiple calls natively. This reference format differs from the exact Hub JSON template, whose code rejects multiple calls in one message.

sources.title: Zipf’s and Heaps’ Laws for Tokens and LLM-generated Texts, Table 3 and Figure 10
sources.publisher: Nikolay Mikhaylovskiy (NTR Labs / Tomsk State University), Findings of EMNLP 2025
sources.evidence: Freshly reopened and visually checked October 27. Table 3 reports Llama-3.2-1B at 1.23B total and 1.23B active. Section 4.1 includes base and original instruction-finetuned models, with BitsAndBytes NF4 used for generation; Figure 10 separately labels L1 and L1i. This is the author’s nominal active-count convention, not a Meta specification or exact per-token census.

sources.title: Compute Where It Counts: Efficient Large Language Models via Learned Granular Sparsity
sources.publisher: Cyris Kissane, Niveditha Iyer and Adam Klein, Crystal AI
sources.evidence: Freshly reopened October 27. Table 1 labels the untouched Llama1B baseline as 1236M active parameters, but Section 4.1 footnote 1 identifies meta-llama/Llama-3.2-1B (base). Section 5.2 separately discusses a CWIC model based on Llama-3.2-1B-Instruct. The 1236M baseline is not treated as a direct Instruct specification; sparse CWIC variants are excluded.

name.note: Matches the exact instruction-tuned BF16 SKU; neither base nor INT4 variant.

family.note: Official SKU belongs to the Llama 3.2 family; llama is the existing catalog family key.

release_date.note: Original BF16 launch date; the later shared-card October date must not replace it.

open_weights.note: Meta released downloadable BF16 weights under its custom license; Hugging Face access is gated.

license.note: Official license name; a custom commercial license, not an OSI assertion.

parameters_b.note: Meta’s exact Instruct card reports the nominal total as 1B (1.23B), including shared embeddings. Retain the published 1.23B precision; the documented SFT/RLHF model and original SKU are distinct from later QLoRA variants.

active_parameters_b.note: Mikhaylovskiy’s Table 3 publishes 1.23B active. Its original Instruct coverage is established by Section 4.1 and Figure 10 (L1i), supported by Meta’s documented tuning and matching SKU architecture. Adopt this nominal research convention; an exact Meta-defined per-token count remains unavailable.

architecture.note: Dense autoregressive Transformer classification follows the reference implementation: 16 layers, 32 query/8 KV heads (GQA), ordinary feedforward projections; shared embeddings are explicit. Structured pruning/distillation describe training, not MoE routing.

context_window.note: Exact BF16 SKU resolves to 131072 tokens. The official INT4 branch is 8192; its limit does not apply here.

modalities.note: Text-only model; generated code is represented as text.

reasoning.note: Reasoning benchmarks and ordinary chain-of-thought prompting do not establish a dedicated reasoning mode. No separate reasoning mode is specified in the inspected card/prompt interface; clear the unsupported false assertion.

tool_call.note: Meta explicitly documents native custom function calls for1B and3B Instruct. Its reference pythonic format supports multiple calls; the exact Hugging Face JSON template rejects multiple calls in one message. Template restrictions are not treated as a model-wide limitation. Meta excludes built-in Brave/Wolfram tools.

description.value: Compact instruction-tuned Llama model for multilingual dialogue and on-device assistants
description.note: Consistent with the documented chat, multilingual and mobile/edge use cases.

patch.notes: Original BF16 Instruct checkpoint. Meta reports approximately 1.23B total parameters with shared embeddings. Active 1.23B follows Mikhaylovskiy’s published nominal convention for the original base/Instruct models, not an exact Meta per-token count. Dense Transformer with GQA, produced through structured pruning and distillation. Context is 131,072 tokens; later official INT4 variants use 8,192. Native custom function calling is documented for 1B; dedicated reasoning-mode support is undisclosed. Meta reference pythonic calls can contain multiple functions; the Hub JSON template handles one call per message.

summary: October 27 parameter re-audit retains Meta’s nominal 1.23B total and verifies 1.23B active under Mikhaylovskiy’s research convention. Visually checked Table 3 and the Instruct-identifying Figure 10; reopened the exact Meta card, SKU and launch, and searched for newer developer disclosures. CWIC’s 1236M baseline is identified as the base checkpoint, so it is not preferred for this Instruct record. Exact per-token participation remains unspecified. Preserve all 12 unrelated assessments and the original audit’s other patch values. No weights downloaded.
